questions.statement: Complete the sentence: "Maria _____ breakfast at 7:00 every morning."

options.feedback: Incorrecto. "Have" is used with I, you, we, they; not with third person singular.
Incorrecto. "Is having" is present continuous, not simple present for habitual actions.
Correcto. "Has" is the correct third person singular form of "have".
Correcto. Third person singular requires "has".

questions.explanation:
Uso del present simple con tercera persona del singular: verbos con -s/-es.

questions.statement: What is the English word for "cuaderno"?

options.feedback: Incorrecto. "Book" means "libro", not "cuaderno".
Incorrecto. "Paper" is "papel", a different object.
Correcto. "Notebook" is the correct translation for "cuaderno".
Incorrecto. "Pencil" means "lápiz".

questions.explanation:
Vocabulario básico: objetos escolares y su equivalencia en inglés.

questions.statement: Choose the correct question: "_____ you from Guatemala?"

options.feedback: Incorrecto. "Is" is used with third person singular (he, she, it).
Correcto. "Are" is the correct form of "to be" for the pronoun "you".
Incorrecto. "Am" is used with first person singular "I".
Incorrecto. "Be" is the base form, not used as an auxiliary in questions.

questions.explanation:
Formación de preguntas con el verbo "to be" según el sujeto.

questions.statement: The Guatemalan flag has two colors: blue and _____.

options.feedback: Incorrecto. The flag has blue and white, not green.
Incorrecto. Red is not in the Guatemalan flag.
Correcto. The Guatemalan flag has vertical blue and white stripes.
Incorrecto. Yellow is not part of the national flag.

questions.explanation:
Vocabulario básico de colores aplicado a la identidad nacional.

questions.statement:
Read the text and answer: "Tikal is an ancient Mayan city in the Petén jungle. Thousands of tourists visit it every year."
What is Tikal?

options.feedback: Incorrecto. The text says it is an "ancient Mayan city".
Incorrecto. Tikal is in the jungle, not on the coast.

options.text: An ancient Mayan city in the jungle.
options.feedback: Correcto. The text explicitly states this.
Incorrecto. Tikal is not a volcano.

questions.explanation:
Comprensión de lectura básica: extracción de información explícita de un texto corto.

---

questions.statement: Choose the correct sentence: "Right now, the students _____ in the classroom."

options.feedback: Incorrecto. "Study" is present simple, for habitual actions, not for "right now".
Incorrecto. "Studies" is third person present simple.
Correcto. "Are studying" is present continuous, used for actions happening now.
Incorrecto. "Is" is singular, but "students" is plural.

questions.explanation:
Diferenciación entre presente simple (hábitos) y presente continuo (acciones en curso).

---

questions.statement: "The market is _____ the church and the park."

options.feedback: Incorrecto. "On" indicates a surface, not a position between two places.
Incorrecto. This would mean the market is on one side facing both.
Correcto. "Between" is used when something is in the middle of two other things.
Incorrecto. "Next to" would mean it is beside one, not both.

questions.explanation:
Uso de preposiciones de lugar para describir ubicaciones en contextos cotidianos.

questions.statement:
Read the text: "Pepián is a traditional Guatemalan stew. It is made with chicken, vegetables, and a rich sauce. People usually eat it with rice and tortillas."
What is Pepián?

options.feedback: Incorrecto. Pepián is a stew, not a fruit.
Incorrecto. It is a food dish.

options.text: A traditional stew with chicken and vegetables.
options.feedback: Correcto. The text says it is a stew with these ingredients.
Incorrecto. Pepián is a food, not an instrument.

questions.explanation:
Comprensión de lectura: identificación del tema central de un texto descriptivo sobre gastronomía.

questions.statement: Complete with the past simple: "Yesterday, we _____ (visit) the Antigua Guatemala ruins."

options.feedback: Incorrecto. "Visit" is present tense, not past.
Incorrecto. "Visiting" is a gerund or present participle.
Correcto. "Visited" is the past simple form of "visit".
Incorrecto. "Visits" is third person present simple.

questions.explanation:
Formación del pasado simple en verbos regulares: adición de -ed.

questions.statement: "I need _____ information about the tour to Lake Atitlán."

options.feedback: Incorrecto. "Information" is uncountable; we cannot use "a" with uncountable nouns.
Incorrecto. "An" is also for singular countable nouns.
Correcto. "Some" is used with uncountable nouns in affirmative sentences.
Incorrecto. "Many" is used with countable plural nouns.

questions.explanation:
Uso de cuantificadores con sustantivos contables e incontables.

questions.statement: "She _____ study medicine at the University of San Carlos."

options.feedback: Incorrecto. "Will" and "going to" are not used together.
Correcto. "Is going to" expresses a future plan or intention.
Correcto. Structure: subject + is/are/am + going to + verb base.
Incorrecto. Missing the auxiliary and "going".

questions.explanation:
Uso de "going to" para expresar planes e intenciones futuras.

---

questions.statement: "In Guatemala, you _____ be 18 years old to vote."

options.feedback: Incorrecto. "Can" expresses ability or possibility, not obligation.
Correcto. "Must" expresses obligation or requirement.
Incorrecto. "Should" expresses advice or recommendation, not a legal requirement.
Incorrecto. "Could" is the past of "can" or a polite possibility.

questions.explanation:
Distinción entre verbos modales: obligación (must), consejo (should) y posibilidad (can/could).

questions.statement:
Read the text: "Eco-tourism in Guatemala is growing. Travelers visit the cloud forests of the Sierra de las Minas to see birds like the quetzal. This type of tourism helps protect the environment and supports local communities."
What is the main benefit of eco-tourism mentioned?

options.feedback: Incorrecto. The text does not mention the cost.
Incorrecto. The text mentions environmental protection and community support.

options.text: It helps protect the environment and supports local communities.
options.feedback: Correcto. The text explicitly mentions both benefits.

options.text: It is the only way to see the quetzal.
options.feedback: Incorrecto. There might be other ways.

questions.explanation:
Comprensión de lectura: identificación de beneficios y propósitos en textos argumentativos cortos.

questions.statement: "Lake Atitlán is one of _____ lakes in the world."

options.feedback: Incorrecto. "More beautiful" is comparative, used to compare two things.
Correcto. "The most beautiful" is the superlative form, used for one among many.
Incorrecto. Missing the definite article "the".
Incorrecto. "Beautiful" uses "more/most" not -er/-est.

questions.explanation:
Formación de superlativos en adjetivos largos: the most + adjective.

questions.statement: "The plane to Guatemala City will _____ at 10:00 PM."

options.feedback: Correcto. "Take off" means to leave the ground and begin flying.
Incorrecto. "Get up" means to rise from bed.
Correcto. This phrasal verb is used for aircraft departure.
Incorrecto. "Go on" means to continue.

questions.explanation:
Comprensión de phrasal verbs comunes relacionados con viajes y transporte.

questions.statement: "If you visit Semuc Champey, you _____ (see) beautiful turquoise pools."

options.feedback: Correcto. The first conditional uses "if + present, will + verb".
Incorrecto. "Would see" is used in the second conditional (unreal present).
Correcto. The first conditional expresses a real possibility in the future.
Incorrecto. Past tense is not used in the result clause of a first conditional.

questions.explanation:
Formación del primer condicional: if + presente simple, will + verbo base.

questions.statement: You want to invite a friend to visit Guatemala. Which of the following is the most appropriate way to start an informal email?
questions.context: Writing an email to a friend.

options.feedback: Incorrecto. This is a formal salutation, not appropriate for a friend.
Incorrecto. This is used for formal letters or references.
Correcto. "Hi" + name is an appropriate informal salutation for a friend.
Incorrecto. This is semi-formal, not for a close friend.

questions.explanation:
Diferenciación entre registro formal e informal en la escritura de correos electrónicos.

questions.statement:
You see a sign at the Pacaya Volcano: "WARNING: Active volcanic area. Follow marked trails only. Do not approach the crater."
What does this sign mean?

options.text: You can camp anywhere on the volcano.
options.feedback: Incorrecto. The sign says to follow marked trails.

options.text: The volcano is extinct and safe to explore freely.
options.feedback: Incorrecto. It says "Active volcanic area".

options.text: You must stay on the trails and keep away from the crater.
options.feedback: Correcto. This is the direct meaning of the warning.

options.text: You can approach the crater if you are with a guide.
options.feedback: Incorrecto. The sign says "Do not approach" without exceptions.

questions.explanation:
Comprensión de letreros y avisos de seguridad en contextos turísticos y naturales.

questions.statement: Change to passive voice: "Farmers grow coffee in many regions of Guatemala."

options.text: Coffee grows in many regions of Guatemala.
options.feedback: Incorrecto. This changes the meaning; "grows" is intransitive here.

options.text: Coffee is grow by farmers in Guatemala.
options.feedback: Incorrecto. "Grow" should be "grown" (past participle).

options.text: Coffee is grown in many regions of Guatemala.
options.feedback: Correcto. Passive voice: subject (coffee) + is + past participle (grown).

options.text: Farmers are grown coffee in Guatemala.
options.feedback: Incorrecto. The agent and subject are confused.

questions.explanation:
Transformación de oraciones activas a pasivas utilizando el verbo "to be" + participio pasado.

questions.statement:
Read the sentence: "Despite its small size, Guatemala is a megadiverse country with an incredible variety of ecosystems, from mangroves to cloud forests."
What does "megadiverse" most likely mean?

options.feedback: Incorrecto. "Small size" is mentioned separately; "megadiverse" does not mean small.

options.text: Having many different types of plants and animals.
options.feedback: Correcto. "Mega" = large, "diverse" = variety of species and ecosystems.

options.text: Having many different types of plants and animals.
options.feedback: Correcto. The context mentions variety of ecosystems.

options.text: Having only one type of climate.
options.feedback: Incorrecto. The text lists different ecosystems (mangroves, cloud forests).

questions.explanation:
Inferencia del significado de palabras a partir del contexto y la composición léxica.
